photograph.author: OAR/National Undersea Research Program (NURP).
photograph.description: The lobster's large claw can crush crabs, clams and fingers. Homarus americanus. Atlantic Ocean, offshore Maine. 1975 November.
photograph.mediaType: Reference photograph/micrograph; imaging and identification require individual review
photograph.review: Actual retained reference viewed and compared with the final side/front/top, detail and action sheets on October24; source identity is not a new independent determination.
photograph.changes: Resized inside 1000 px, flattened and JPEG encoded; no generative alteration.
photograph.captionLicense: External Commons description text; retain source page and its applicable license
photograph.identityScope: NOAA/NURP source labels Homarus americanus offshore Maine, November1975. The selected warm red/olive rendering follows this authentic lit photograph, not a cooked animal or all natural color variation. Sex, lighting and dimensions are not independently redetermined.

sources.title: FAO/Holthuis1991 — selected Homarus key and American species figure
sources.scope: Actual PDFpage8 printed57 Fig104/105 and page9 printed58 Fig106 rendered/read. Naked unequal palms, usual ventral rostral tooth, serial abdomen and tail fan are selected morphological context; no calibrated anatomy, rate or physiology.

sources.title: Macmillan1975 — A physiological analysis of walking in the American lobster
sources.scope: Primary-paper PubMed abstract read only, not full experimental paper. Forward stepping of four walking pairs and variable phase relationships provide context. This model uses a fixed illustrative sequence, without original EMG, transducer signals, measured joint coordinates or fitted gait.

sources.title: Fisheries and Oceans Canada — American lobster
sources.scope: Institutional species description read for variable brown/olive cuticle, five pereiopod pairs including major chelae, pleopods and a central telson with four uropod lobes. Selected warm-lit NOAA phenotype remains separate from typical coloration; not measured material or physiology.

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A separately proportioned robust carapace, a ventral rostral tooth, one broader crusher and a longer-fingered cutter, eight supported articulated walking limbs with small P2/P3 claws, six serial abdominal plates and a central telson with four uropod lobes replace the generic draft.
shape.remaining: Rostral tooth variability, fine cuticular detail, setal structures, mouthparts, joint axes, claw dentition and internal physiology remain incomplete/unmeasured. The red/olive selection does not represent all natural coloration, and the photograph cannot calibrate illumination or reflectance. Sex/age are not independently redetermined; modified first pleopods are omitted.

surface.changed: A warm red/olive selected phenotype follows the authentic lit NOAA/NURP source image. Smooth naked palms, fine varied cuticle and pale seams replace the undifferentiated tan surface; no generated photograph or measured material map is used.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, without calibrated optics, scan or full natural variation. Rostral tooth variability, fine cuticular detail, setal structures, mouthparts, joint axes, claw dentition and internal physiology remain incomplete/unmeasured. The red/olive selection does not represent all natural coloration, and the photograph cannot calibrate illumination or reflectance. Sex/age are not independently redetermined; modified first pleopods are omitted.

movement.changed: A short authored forward support/recovery bout, retained chela and antennule gestures, finger opening, quiet support and partial local tail/fan flex. No force, fitted stride, actual escape displacement, fluid flow, muscle, heart/gill or ingestion mechanism.
movement.remaining: No measured coordinates, natural playback rate, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, muscle, food contact, ingestion, sensory physiology or independent biological validation. Fixed-length/support checks establish internal software consistency only.

sourceAssessment: The authentic offshore-Maine1975 NOAA/NURP photograph and actual FAO printed57/58 figures were viewed. DFO/USGS/NOAA account context distinguishes the typical species range and variable pigmentation from the selected image. Macmillan1975 primary-paper abstract describes variable forward stepping; only qualitative context is used, not original recordings or fitted coordinates.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Kept the usually present ventral rostral tooth separate from the European species' absent-tooth profile.
Reduced coarse camouflage and increased palm surface resolution after top-view comparison exposed star-like pigment artifacts.
Used unequal palm widths and shorter crusher fingers; retained all surfaces through behavior/reset.
Bound the three anatomy markers to the carapace, actual crusher palm and moving fan, and corrected the inherited label names.

assessmentRubric.identity: Accepted species-rank concept checked; photographed organism remains source-labelled
assessmentRubric.body: Substantial initial correction; unmeasured dimensions and incomplete fine diagnostic anatomy
assessmentRubric.texture: Distinct selected numerical surface; optics and microanatomy remain illustrative
assessmentRubric.movement: Working qualitative supported articulation; empirical rate/dynamics unvalidated

reviewMethod: 55 actual final nonblank side/front/top, enlarged and action/posture states inspected individually on labelled sheets against the authentic photograph and scoped sources. Superseded frames excluded. Qualitative author assessment, not independent expert certification.

samples.status: Actual final frame visually inspected on labelled comparison sheets; qualitative author assessment
samples.finding: A separately proportioned robust carapace, a ventral rostral tooth, one broader crusher and a longer-fingered cutter, eight supported articulated walking limbs with small P2/P3 claws, six serial abdominal plates and a central telson with four uropod lobes replace the generic draft. A warm red/olive selected phenotype follows the authentic lit NOAA/NURP source image. Smooth naked palms, fine varied cuticle and pale seams replace the undifferentiated tan surface; no generated photograph or measured material map is used. Remaining: Rostral tooth variability, fine cuticular detail, setal structures, mouthparts, joint axes, claw dentition and internal physiology remain incomplete/unmeasured. The red/olive selection does not represent all natural coloration, and the photograph cannot calibrate illumination or reflectance. Sex/age are not independently redetermined; modified first pleopods are omitted.
